title: Install or initialize Pratica
summary: Deploy, verify, or recover the user-owned content-addressed Pratica CLI and Chancery selector, then separately initialize or diagnose its private negotiation database and Nucleus readiness.
use_when: Pratica should be installed or updated for this macOS user.
The installed binary, provider selector, release identity, database schema, integrity, private permissions, Nucleus readiness, or immutable toolsets should be checked.
A new empty Pratica database should be explicitly initialized.
do_not_use_when: The task is ordinary negotiation or agreement inspection.
A foreign or tampered selector or release should be overwritten, or storage should be initialized or deleted as a deployment side effect.
Deployment, initialization, or another installed-state change has not been explicitly authorized.
outcome: A version-matched content-addressed local release whose command and sole providers/pratica selector follow one current release, an explicitly initialized schema-one database, or an evidence-backed readiness diagnosis.
effects: Deployment stages immutable binary, deployer, manifest, and Pratica-owned Chancery bytes, then changes the current release selected by both public surfaces.
Deployment writes ~/.local/bin/pratica and one Chancery provider selector but starts no service, submits no Nucleus job, and never opens or changes the domain database.
A separate init creates schema one; doctor reads schema, integrity, permissions, Nucleus health, and immutable toolset readiness without negotiating terms.
authority: Pratica owns its releases, current and previous selectors, command selector, providers/pratica selector, schema initialization, and database integrity checks.
Nucleus remains separately authoritative for execution and authentication; deployment does not restart or reconfigure it.
The operator separately chooses whether and where to initialize persistent negotiation state.
success: The candidate and provider versions match, the exact staged release manifest matches every component, and both public selectors resolve through one current release.
Identical redeployment is idempotent, an update retains the prior valid release, and failed post-switch smoke restores binary and provider views together.
The deployer refuses foreign, symbolic, traversal, fabricated, incomplete, or tampered owned state and creates no database or sidecar.
After separate initialization, doctor proves schema-one integrity, content/seal invariants, private permissions, strict Nucleus readiness, and all three immutable Pratica toolsets.
failure_and_recovery: A pre-commit deployment failure restores current, previous, command, and provider selectors; inspect the reported owned paths before retrying.
After a committed domain-canary failure, preserve its evidence and redeploy the exact previous packaged binary/deployer only when schema compatibility remains safe.
Do not bypass manifest or selector refusal, initialize missing state implicitly, rewrite database history, or restart Nucleus to recover a Pratica attempt.
privacy: Release and provider bytes contain no negotiated terms or source snapshots; the private database and Nucleus records may contain both.
Deployment must never package, inspect, print, copy, migrate, or delete the Pratica database.
steps: Build and validate a green Pratica candidate without changing installed state.
Run the product deployer with the absolute release binary and inspect version, current release, command selector, provider selector, and manifest.
Initialize storage only as a separate explicit action, then run doctor and installed Chancery discovery.
Use the documented contract-only CRM canary when a real domain canary is intended.
checkpoints: Pratica installs no daemon, LaunchAgent, schedule, source crawler, or direct Codex path.
No deployer operation creates, opens, migrates, backs up, or deletes negotiation state.
All three toolset identities and meanings remain immutable and Nucleus-compatible.
adaptation: Use --database or PRATICA_DATABASE when the default private application-support database is not intended.
Treat a future schema change as a separate quiescent backup, migration, and database-aware rollback project.
stop_when: Candidate identity, provider version, exact tree, selector ownership, schema, Nucleus compatibility, or privacy cannot be proved.
An active model-assisted command or pending tool call makes the intended maintenance boundary unsafe.
Initialization, retry, release publication, or target-system change is being inferred from deployment authority.
does_not_authorize: Publishing a release, replacing foreign state, retrying a negotiation attempt, or deleting retained releases or contracts.
Changing Nucleus, Chancery, CRM, a stewarded system, or Semantics state.

consumers.statement: The local operator may deploy or diagnose Pratica and may separately initialize one intentionally selected empty negotiation ledger.

preconditions.statement: Deployment has explicit authority and a regular absolute candidate whose version matches the provider; doctor requires compatible Nucleus readiness to prove model-assisted operation.

inputs.statement: Deployment consumes the candidate binary and packaged provider/deployer bytes; init consumes a selected database path; doctor reads the selected database and Nucleus readiness.

outputs.statement: Outputs are one content-addressed installed release, one separately initialized schema-one database, or readiness evidence for storage, permissions, Nucleus, and immutable toolsets.

data_semantics.statement: Installed current and previous name validated release generations; deployment success is separate from database existence, Nucleus readiness, and negotiation-domain success.

identity_and_units.statement: Content digest identifies the exact release tree, provider release must equal binary version, and database schema plus three toolset identities are separately versioned.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: A successful deployment publishes the complete validated owned release through both selectors; doctor reads current local storage and live Nucleus readiness at invocation.

access.statement: The operation uses local filesystem and shell authority over Pratica-owned paths and read-only Nucleus health; it refuses foreign, symbolic, fabricated, or tampered state.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Redeployment is idempotent, update retains a valid previous release, failure restores both public selectors, and deployment never opens or changes negotiation state.

operational_limits.statement: Deployment starts no daemon or schedule and creates no database; initialization and any attempt retry remain separate explicit operations.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Candidate and provider versions match exactly, doctor requires Nucleus execution contract 1 and immutable version-one toolsets, and schema change requires a separate migration and rollback project.

reliances.statement: Doctor relies on Nucleus health and capability reporting to prove model-assisted Pratica readiness without transferring negotiation authority.
